second_answer_attack.resolution: A lower intracellular chloride concentration would strengthen the hyperpolarizing chloride gradient and is the opposite of what reduced KCC2 extrusion causes. SLC12A5 loss raises intracellular chloride and shifts the chloride equilibrium potential to less negative values, weakening GABA-A inhibition.

blind_audit.rationale: KCC2 normally extrudes potassium and chloride from mature neurons and helps maintain a low intracellular chloride concentration. Loss of KCC2 function shifts the chloride equilibrium potential to less negative values, weakening the hyperpolarizing effect of GABA-A receptor opening. Strongest alternative resolved: A lower intracellular chloride concentration would strengthen the hyperpolarizing chloride gradient and is the opposite of what reduced KCC2 extrusion causes. SLC12A5 loss raises intracellular chloride and shifts the chloride equilibrium potential to less negative values, weakening GABA-A inhibition.
